title: Ten Tabletop Games for fans of Dark Souls
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hVVP3uqEbXg

Before recommending anything, Daniel (@dungeondive) defines what he is actually chasing: exploration and discovery, interesting lore, itemisation deep enough to support builds, combat that is more than rolling dice, and above all a mood. The ten picks are then measured against that list rather than against Dark Souls' surface.

Two are hard to find — *Dark Light: Memento Mori*, a Dark Souls/Diablo hybrid with one of the only genuine dodge-roll mechanisms in a board game, and *Forgotten Depths*, chosen for exploration driven by the shapes of rooms and corridors, plus an expansion that is simply a deck of bonfire conversations. The rest are gettable: *The Restless* for its 500-odd hand-drawn cards, *Corrupted Crypts* print-on-demand from The Game Crafter, and *Kernathalis* from Black Oath as the mega-dungeon pick.

*Vermis* is the outlier and arguably the closest match — a guidebook for a video game that does not exist, recommended as esoteric fiction or a solo oracle. *Loom* pulls the same metatextual trick but ships an actual game, with a VHS and vinyl soundtrack for a film that never was. *Mork Borg* earns its place on humour as much as grime, and *Rune* (with *Reap*) models bonfires, respawns and world-state clocks directly. *Dungeons of Doria* closes on pure loot — gear with stat requirements you level up to meet.

----

Which matters more in a Souls-like tabletop game — mechanically modelling the bonfire and respawn loop, or just nailing the mood?
